title: Refuse prompt edits that contradict verdict rules in verify.rs
summary: Add to crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs a table of verdict rules (D-numbered evidence rules and judged output fields) plus a check that compares a proposed edit of verifier prompt text against them. A contradicting instruction, or a missing required field, is refused with the rule named. Audience: Athena maintainers whose prompt edits currently surface only as verifier rejections.

defaults_applied.how: Implemented in Rust with Rust tests.
New tests; cargo test and clippy must pass.
Criteria run tests showing refusal and acceptance.
Verifier runs cargo test, clippy, fmt --check.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs (D43, D63, D115 evidence rules; finding construction near line 601), crates/athena-context/prompts/*.md and crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs and outputs.rs for prompt composition and structured fields. The check is a pure function over prompt text and a static rule table; it runs at reading/plan admission when the request edits a prompt file. Nothing is added as a record or data file, so check_record_file/AnyRecord are not touched. The property is measured directly by scanning the actual prompt text for contradicting phrases and required field names.

Scope is limited to verify.rs (as the request's Files line says) plus its in-file tests; wiring into the reading and plan critic briefs is only done if a minimal hook exists already, else the function is exposed for them.
The check uses simple phrase and field-name matching against rules registered in a table, with each rule carrying an id like D43 so the refusal names it.
The prompt budget test is unchanged because no prompt file is edited.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new unit test in crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs feeds a prompt edit that contradicts a D-numbered verdict rule (e.g. telling the verifier to accept uncited commands against D43) and asserts it is refused with the rule id in the message; run `cargo test -p athena-core verify`.
A new unit test feeds a consistent prompt edit and asserts it is accepted; run `cargo test -p athena-core verify`.
A new test asserts a prompt that omits a field the judging code requires is refused naming the missing field; run `cargo test -p athena-core verify`.
The real current prompts in crates/athena-context/prompts/ pass the new check (a test runs it over include_str! of verifier.md), so no existing behavior is refused; run `cargo test`.
The change refuses more prompt edits than before and the higher refusal rate is intended: expected 5% of newly refused readings.
The prompt budget test and the full suite pass, with `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy` clean.
The git diff touches only crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs and no governance files (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows).

out_of_scope: Editing any prompt file under crates/athena-context/prompts/
Changing existing verdict rules D43/D63/D115 behavior
hard_reason: Adds a refusal check that blocks dispatch when a prompt conflicts with verdict rules, so it changes a gate and the pipeline that judges jobs.
